An ERP's ETO module records the engineering BOM, routings, and transactions. It doesn't recalculate coverage and capacity across every order when a change lands, or rank what to fix first. Pelico sits on top of the ERP, reads its data, and leaves the transactional records where they are.

It's hard to tell what's truly at risk, or what protecting one program costs another. There’s a nagging feeling that you’re about to be blindsided.

Manufacturing orchestration is an approach to operations execution that treats disruption as the normal state, not the exception. When something slips, teams know what it breaks, coordinate the response, and make the trade-offs before a delivery is at risk.
A slipped PO shows every work order, site, and customer order it touches, across BOM levels and supplier tiers. No spreadsheets needed to bridge systems.

Leaders see what's at risk, size the impact of each option, and know what protecting one program costs another.

Do your buyers work shortages in due-date order, or by the revenue and delivery each one puts at risk?
Every missing part ranked by downstream revenue and delivery impact.

Rank shortages by what they hold back, not by due date. A late part blocking a high-value customer order matters more than an earlier one that holds nothing. Pelico ranks every shortage by the revenue and deliveries it puts at risk, so buyers and planners work the costliest one first.

Safety stock builds because telling a customer "no" costs more than holding it. Pelico ties live inventory to the production it serves, so every defer, cancel, or rebalance decision carries its delivery impact.

Tie each inventory decision to the production it supports. Stock covering a near-term order stays; stock with no demand behind it is a candidate to defer, cancel, or move. In Pelico, every open order carries both its cash exposure and its delivery impact.
What's the best way to know if an engine can be inducted before all the parts arrive?

Check each short part's expected arrival against the gate that needs it. If every part lands before its gate, inducting now protects the slot and the customer date. If one won't, the engine sits disassembled waiting, and deferring is usually the better call. Pelico runs that check for every engine in the queue, so you can induct, defer, or induct with risk on real dates.
Repair priority by TAT and revenue
Score every open service order on contractual TAT, customer priority, and revenue, so planners send parts to the repair that protects the most, not the oldest job.
How can we prioritize repairs by TAT and revenue when the ERP allocates parts first in, first out?

Most ERP and MRO systems allocate first in, first out, and they have no way to weigh a contractual TAT or an AOG against job age. Fixing it means scoring every open service order on TAT, customer priority, and revenue, then moving parts where they protect the most commitments. Pelico runs that scoring on top of your ERP, and planners approve each reallocation.

Put the holds in the same list as the rest of the WIP, with the age and value of each, so customer support chases the ones blocking the most revenue first. Pelico tracks every unit waiting on quote approval and ties it to its TAT and customer, so holds stop hiding in email threads.

This aerospace MRO manufacturer was losing productivity, decision quality, collaboration, and revenue to inaccurate data in its ERP. With Pelico’s manufacturing orchestration platform, it improved its data hygiene from 53% to 93% within eight weeks, and made clean data a cornerstone for daily decisions.

A late supplier date never stays on one PO. Pelico's AI agents trace it through the part and the work order to the customer order it puts at risk, then bring it to the right owner with what's missing, what's blocked, and the revenue on the line. Your team acts before the delivery date slips.
Ranks shortages by delivery and revenue impact. Lays out the recovery options and their trade-offs, and flags each one to the team that owns it.
